newsitem.title: UK: Avalon Oil raises cash to finance Russian venture.
newsitem.headline: Avalon Oil raises cash to finance Russian venture.

text.p: U.S.-based exploration and production company Avalon Oil said on Friday it had raised around 31.7 million pounds ($50.5 million) to finance a Russian joint venture with the world's largest natural gas company.
Oklahoma-based Avalon raised the sum through a placement of shares on London's Alternative Investment Market (AIM) which capitalised the company at 76 million pounds.
The joint venture is with Orenburggazprom, a subsidiary of Russian gas monopoly RAO Gazprom, which accounts for nearly a quarter of the world's gas reserves.
Avalon will hold a 49 percent stake in the venture, Stimul, set up to explore for known oil reserves in the Orenburg field in southern Russia. The Gazprom unit holds the rest.

"The proceeds of the placing will now enable Avalon Oil to make its necessary contribution to Stimul, and develop the significant proven oil reserves of the Orenburg field economically," said Avalon's chairman John Wieczorek.

Avalon is following an increasingly chosen path. Earlier this month, a unit of Melrose Energy Plc sought an AIM listing to raise money for a Siberian oil deal while JKX Oil & Gas Plc plans a rights issue to secure funding for oil and gas projects in Ukraine and Georgia.

"The Russian oil industry is desperate for capital and technology and one shouldn't be surprised to see a spate of similar deals over the next several few years," said Nick Clayton, analyst with Dresdner Kleinwort Benson.
Stimul has a licence running to 2018 to develop and produce proven and probable oil reserves of 371 million barrels and associated gas reserves of 389 million standard cubic feet.

Current production is 2,850 barrels per day (bpd) and after implementation of Avalon's development plans -- it plans to introduce modern technology and exploitation techniques -- output could reach 12,500 bpd this year, the company said.
It hopes to boost production to 18,500 bpd by 1998.
Stimul plans to drill around 160 horizontal producing wells and 51 vertical injection wells over the next six years.
In February Wieczorek had said the Orenburg project would be a "jumping-off point for other projects in Russia". He said the company had been looking at three other Russian fields.

Commenting on the "very successful partnership" with Avalon Oil, Gazprom chairman Rem Viakhirev said: "The new methods allowed us to start commercial production of oil with positive economic efficiency of development".

He said Gazprom would look at further joint ventures following its success with Avalon and earlier with Germany's Wintershall. The link up with BASF unit Wintershall involved a gas marketing venture selling Russian gas in Western Europe.
Avalon's shares have been placed at 100 pence each by Henderson Crosthwaite Corporate Finance and dealings are expected to commence on April 1.
